note: Two separate vocabularies. Source-authority tags describe how well a profile field or fact is sourced. Evidence tiers describe how a claim is backed. An id never appears in both.

source_authority_tags.meaning: Manufacturer primary document, such as a data sheet, data catalog or users manual.
First-party-adjacent material, such as an edited reproduction of an in-house technical document.
Service or hardware documentation, such as a service manual or schematic.
Community documentation or a community measurement. A lead that needs a cross-check.
An emulator is not hardware evidence; lead only. A value backed only by this tag must be recorded as unknown-default-chosen.
source_authority_tags.where_allowed: notes and discrepancy leads, never as the tag of a profile field

source_authority_tags.meaning: Derived by the project from cited sources. The derivation is stated and can be wrong.
Chosen by the owner and recorded in the Decision Register.
Chosen by the project under the owner's delegation and recorded in the Decision Register.
The truth is unknown. A default was chosen; the evidence that would resolve it and the trigger to revisit are recorded.

evidence_tiers.meaning: The expected value is taken from a cited source document.
A public test vector with documented provenance and rights.
A project-authored diagnostic program with a recorded recipe.
Agreement with an independently written implementation. Agreement with a shared core does not count.
Owner-approved physical measurement of real hardware (D10).
Repeated runs give identical output. Establishes repeatability, not accuracy.
A guest program makes observable progress on the named profile.
Behavior of the installed package as consumed by a separate host program.
